hints: Focus on what makes a propagation step special, a radical is used up and a new radical is made to keep the chain going.
Check each equation for radicals, you need exactly one radical dot on the left and one radical dot on the right.
Remember chlorination does not stop at one Cl, think about what happens when the Cl radical attacks the monochloro product again.
walkthrough:
**Recall the three stages of free radical substitution**

Think of it like a relay race. Initiation creates radicals, propagation passes the radical on, termination joins radicals together.

Propagation rule:
$$\text{radical + molecule} \rightarrow \text{new molecule + new radical}$$

**Apply the rule to chlorination of ethane**

The two normal propagation steps for the first substitution are hydrogen abstraction then chlorine capture.
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + \text{Cl}• \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5• + \text{HCl}$$
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5• + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}•$$

**Spot further substitution as valid propagation**

Once $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ forms, it can react again with $\text{Cl}•$ in exactly the same way to give dichloro products. That is still propagation because one radical in gives one radical out.
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}• \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Cl}• + \text{HCl}$$

options.A: This is molecule + radical going to molecule + radical. One Cl radical is consumed and one new carbon radical is formed, so the chain continues. This is the first step of further chlorination of chloroethane to dichloroethane, a perfectly valid propagation.
options.B: This has one radical on each side, but the products are wrong. Cl radical abstracts H to make HCl, not to make C2H5Cl directly, and H dot is far too high in energy to form. The correct step is C2H6 + Cl dot to C2H5 dot + HCl.
options.C: This also has one radical on each side, but H dot is not a chain carrier in alkane chlorination. H dot is never produced in the correct propagation steps, so it cannot be a reactant here. Students who just count radicals without checking the species fall for this.
options.D: Here two radicals combine to make a single neutral molecule with no radicals left. That is the definition of a termination step, not propagation. It stops the chain rather than continuing it.
